sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered to take action over odours Milpitas, an affluent city in California's Silicon Valley tech hub, has an odour problem.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: For decades, residents have had to endure rank smells wafting from industrial sites, among them a 342-acre landfill.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "When I first moved here, I could not open my window for over 10 years," says Chia-Ling Kong, an engineer for a tech firm who lives around half a mile from the dump.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: While things have got better in recent years, Kong says she and her neighbours must still contend with around "two or three hours of bad smells a day".
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Perhaps befitting Silicon Valley, the community is putting its hopes in technology.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The operators of Newby Island landfill have been ordered by local authorities to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure the chemicals responsible for bad odours.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: They have also been told to automate the collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Kong is optimistic a data-driven approach will make a difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Hopefully with this continuous monitoring, it makes it easier to pinpoint problems at the moment it starts." The operators of the landfill say they are committed to operating it safely and protecting air quality.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Just like in Milpitas, where Kong is part of a citizen's campaign against the odours, communities around the world are raising a stink about bad smells making day-to-day life miserable.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Sometimes a rubbish dump is to blame, or it might be a sewage treatment works, or a reeking factory.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: When the complaints start stacking up, resolving them is not always simple.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Many countries have no regulations in place dictating how to manage smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In the US, for example, the Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This leaves states and local governments to take charge of the issue.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Urban sprawl is often part of the problem, bringing communities closer to stinky facilities that may historically have been kept at a distance.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This is creating more demand for technologies to monitor and prevent smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour consultant Micheal Bull says people are increasingly concerned about neighbourhood stinks.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "You're getting developments being built nearer to odorous processes… as land has become more valuable, there is also infilling," Bull says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: He is speaking about his experiences in the UK, but it's a similar story in many parts of the world.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites are among the most difficult to resolve The technologies used to tackle industrial pongs generally fall into three categories: they absorb odours; convert them into something less smelly through a chemical reaction; or burn them away.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Experts on fixing industrial odours say that the best technologies, when used correctly, can remove 90% or more of the target compounds responsible for smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But this can be expensive and some operators opt for simpler and cheaper solutions.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: These include masking odours from landfill or sewage processing by spraying giant quantities of deodorisers.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Odour experts contacted for this article were dubious about the effectiveness of such industrial scale air fresheners.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "In my view they're not likely to change the odours," says Bull, who likens them to fabric conditioner.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Bad smells from waste sites – a common cause of complaints – are among the stinkiest and most difficult to resolve, according to Carlos Diaz, an environmental consultant based in Spain.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Landfill is difficult to treat because you have a very large surface," he says.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: In some places at least, technology is making a real difference.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Residents in Des Moines, Iowa, have long complained of the so-called Eastside Funk, a putrid scent that residents report drifts over parts of the city.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: A study commissioned by city authorities showed that a trio of industrial meat companies were among culprits.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Within 10 miles, there's about half a million people," says Dalton Jacobus, who works in the Department of Neighborhood Services.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "If the winds are out of the wrong direction, 100,000 people can be in the middle of that odour plume." The authorities are now paying around $240,000 (£182,000) a year on technology to track the stink, so they can take action.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "What we wanted to do was build a ring of odour monitors around the facilities that we suspected of emitting odours," says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The monitors, which measure levels of chemical compounds in the air, work in combination with a weather station to provide real-time data on the concentrations that are coming from each facility based off the wind patterns.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: This has put an end to finger pointing about who's to blame each time a smell sparks complaints, says Jacobus.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Smithfield Foods, which operates a meat processing in Des Moines, says it has invested $2m to install a regenerative thermal oxidiser that destroys the chemicals associated with bad smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Even so, the company says it does not believe it is the source of odour complaints.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Before installing the monitors – which some local companies help pay for – officials in Des Moines would drive out to the source of a complaint to sniff the air.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Relying on the human nose to sniff out industrial smells is still commonplace.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Claudia Barrios Obregón from Kunak, the company behind the monitors in Des Moines, says: "Right now, the way that cities control or measure odours is olfactometry: a human panel measures and gives an opinion of what the odour is like.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: But that's not that realistic." The Spanish company's monitors are an example of so-called electronic noses that make it easier to detect smells.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: Whatever technology is used, it can be hard to keep everyone happy, as smells are so subjective.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, the general rule is that the nastier we perceive the odour to be, the more sensitive towards it we are," says Johan Lundström, a professor in the science of smell at the Karolinska Institute in Stockholm, Sweden.
sentences.article_title: Living with a stink? Technology might help

sentences.text: The sixth report of the Covid inquiry is highly critical of the way the government tried to protect people in care settings in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Around 500,000 people were living in care homes at the start of the pandemic – with another million receiving care in their own homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry said action to protect them came too late, causing devastating consequences.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: There were more than 43,000 recorded deaths involving Covid in care homes between March 2020 and July 2022.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Here are the key findings of the 287-page report.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: At the start of the pandemic, the then-health secretary in England, Matt Hancock, said the UK government had placed "a protective ring" around care homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But the inquiry says this was not the case, listing a catalogue of failings.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It says the care sector appeared to be "something of an afterthought".
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: A lack of personal protective equipment (PPE) meant staff had to resort to makeshift workarounds, including bin bags, festival waterproof ponchos and painters' overalls.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The report is also critical of the way hospital patients who may be infected with Covid were moved to care homes to make space for others.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The decision was understandable given the need to free up beds for Covid patients.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But, without sufficient testing, it was important to keep these people separate and isolate them from others in case they were infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Official guidance in March 2020 in England, Wales and Northern Ireland did not request this.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: That, the report says, was a significant oversight.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: When the pandemic started, high levels of staff vacancies and turnover in the social care sector meant that the workforce was "fragile and lacking resilience".
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This undermined the ability of the sector to respond to the pandemic, the inquiry says.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: For example, care homes tend to rely heavily on agency staff who work in a variety of different homes.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But a desire not to have staff going into multiple homes, to reduce the risk of infection transmission, meant staff shortages got even worse.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Financially, care providers struggled too, as the number of people using services dropped.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: And for a sector that uses zero-hours contracts, there was a lack of financial support to help care staff stay off work if there was concern they might be infected.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The response also suffered because of the fragmented nature of the system, with thousands of different providers and services overseen by councils.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It meant the sector was more distant from government than the NHS.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The pandemic, the inquiry said, exposed and exacerbated these existing weaknesses.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The report is clear that precautionary steps taken to restrict visiting, as part of infection control, went too far.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: It acknowledges there was little choice to introduce bans on visitors at the start of the pandemic, saying that was rational.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But as the pandemic progressed, so did the balance between the benefits and harms of restrictions.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Visits are extremely important, allowing loved ones to help residents with everything from personal care to maintaining their mental health.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: By September 2020, evidence suggested visitors posed a "marginal risk" – staff were judged to be the key entry point for infections.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The four UK nations then started to relax their guidance, but many care homes failed to implement this and visiting remained heavily restricted.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This, says the inquiry, resulted in a significant decline in the health and wellbeing of residents.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: CPR (Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation), including chest compressions, can be life-saving if a person's heart has stopped beating.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: But doctors can sometimes opt not to resuscitate people - as can individuals themselves in advance - for example, if the individual is extremely frail or has a life-limiting illness.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This should be done on an individual basis and the use of blanket do not resuscitate orders (DNACPR) is considered unlawful.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry says it heard evidence of GPs imposing blanket DNACPRs on care home residents.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: And it pointed to records showing a sharp increase in orders being put in place – they jumped from 16,800 to 26,500 in the first nine months of the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: This concern mirrors an earlier Care Quality Commission investigation which found evidence of unacceptable and inappropriate DNACPRs being put in place.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: The impact on staff working in care homes was huge, affecting their mental health and wellbeing, the inquiry said.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Some moved into the care homes where they worked, in an attempt to protect residents from infection.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: One care home owner in Wales described how 39 staff moved in for a fortnight at the start of the pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Seeing so many residents die placed an enormous strain on workers, who often had to provide end-of-life care to multiple people at the same time.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: One care home, for example, lost half of its residents over the course of three weeks.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Staff told the inquiry of the deep distress they suffered.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: "Staff were sitting on video calls with families, saying their last goodbye to loved ones.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: That was horrendous… staff were crying with the residents, because it was just so emotional for them," one said.
sentences.article_title: Covid failings in care homes: What the inquiry says

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Seventeen and 18-year-olds can book via the NHS National Booking Service , external if they are already registered with a GP , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine, given as two doses and at least 28 days apart, is being offered to 17 and 18-year-olds in sixth form and students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Within weeks, in Kent, there were 29 confirmed or suspected cases and two deaths.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: That's why the new, one-off campaign is being launched - to help protect those at greatest risk and hopefully prevent something like this from happening again.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Students in their first year of university have a risk that is about seven times higher than that of young people of a similar age who do not go to university, says NHS England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meningitis infections can be spread through close contact - for example through kissing, sharing vapes and drinks or living in close quarters with a person with the bug.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: UK health officials say the risk to 18-year-olds or those entering university or a residential college for the first time is higher because of increased mixing of social groups and shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: MenB infection can cause serious, life-threatening problems including inflammation of the lining of the brain (meningitis) and blood poisoning (sepsis).
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can lead to life-changing disabilities such as amputations, hearing loss and brain damage, and in some cases can be fatal.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: All babies are now offered it.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But it means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Meanwhile, they do want everyone who is eligible to come forward and get the vaccine because it can prevent serious illness.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Each nation has its own plans , external , but all are offering the vaccine to most pupils completing Year 13 or S6 in the summer of 2026 - irrespective of their education plans and including people from this age group who are not currently in school.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Viral meningitis tends to get better on its own within seven to 10 days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It can often be treated at home with plenty of rest, painkillers and anti-sickness medicine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis needs to be treated in hospital.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Outbreaks are thankfully rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Currently, a separate vaccine covering different strains, the MenACWY vaccine, is offered routinely to 14-year-olds.

sentences.text: Hayley lost her job as a teaching assistant last October, after being told she was unfit to work Hayley Locksley was 11 years old when she started her periods and excruciating pain became part of her life.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I used to spend every month in the sick room at school," she says.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley, from Shefford, Bedfordshire, would often pass out from the pain but the doctors' advice was to take paracetamol.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Aged 24, she was diagnosed with endometriosis - a condition that affects one in 10 women, where tissue similar to the lining of the womb grows outside of the uterus.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley says she loved her job working in a nursery, but her employers questioned whether her symptoms were real and asked her to use annual leave to cover sick days.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: After she had surgery for endometriosis, Hayley decided to switch to office work, due to it being less physically demanding.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: But her new colleagues asked why she was spending so long in the toilet.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I had to explain that my bladder sometimes did not empty fully, causing severe pain and horrendous diarrhoea.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: I found the questioning embarrassing and humiliating," she says.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley had her appendix removed because doctors thought that was the issue, until she was diagnosed with endometriosis After having her daughter, who is now aged seven, Hayley decided to pursue her dream of working with children again and became a special needs teaching assistant in a primary school four years ago.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: However, she was placed under review after her sickness absence increased and she lost her job last October, after being told she was unfit to work.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I didn't want to give up my career but my health meant I could no longer continue," she says.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "I now use a walking stick, experience severe back and leg pain, and have fallen numerous times.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "Women should not have to choose between their health and their careers.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Now we need meaningful action," she says.

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "Your absence policy shouldn't be the same as someone who is able-bodied and has no medical condition, you shouldn't be [judged] against that person because it's just not fair." The government says it is working with employers to improve awareness of the condition.

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Firms are keen to explore how they can support women "without their careers being held back", in a "wider shift" towards helping improve health and wellbeing in the workplace, he adds.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: Hayley, Carla and Faye all say they hope employers can show more understanding of endometriosis in the future.
sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.article_title: I lost my job in a primary school due to endometriosis

sentences.text: "Endometriosis has taken so much from me.

sentences.text: I don't want to be in this position.

sentences.text: I loved my job and I worked really hard.

sentences.text: Franklin was a British chemist and crystallographer, whose X-ray diffraction work helped discover the structure of DNA Rosalind Franklin is the only female scientist named in GCSE and National 5 science exam specifications in the UK, according to new research.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: A Cambridge study found that of the 86 scientists named by UK exam boards, the English chemist, whose work in the 1950s helped reveal the structure of DNA, was the only woman.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam specifications set out the skills and knowledge students are expected to have gained by the end of their course and how they will be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Exam boards said there was "a clear need for greater representation in science qualifications".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics from the University of Cambridge, along with institutions in the US and Australia, examined how many women were mentioned in specifications for biology, chemistry, physics, environmental science, geology and astronomy.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Their work, published in the British Educational Research Journal, looked at six exam boards in the UK: At Key Stage 4 and equivalent, including GCSEs and National 5s in Scotland, Franklin was the only woman among the 86 scientists mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: She was also one of three women mentioned at Key Stage 5 and equivalent - including A-levels, AS-levels, National Highers and National Advanced Highers - out of a total of 181 scientists.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Marie Tharp, an American cartographer who created the first map of the floor of the Atlantic ocean in the 1950s, and Inge Lehmann, a Danish seismologist who discovered the existence of the Earth's inner core in the 1930s, both feature in the Cambridge OCR's A-­level Geology.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin, who was named in Cambridge OCR's GCSE Biology and Scottish Highers Biology, produced a famous DNA image known as Photograph 51.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Cambridge scientists Francis Crick and James Watson used the image to work out the following year that DNA has a double-helix structure.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Watson, Crick and Franklin's colleague Maurice Wilkins received the 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Franklin had died four years earlier.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Academics who wrote the paper found that "several major scientific breakthroughs" in specifications were made by women, but they were not explicitly mentioned.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The paper said: "Many of the scientific discoveries and explanations were developed in the 1800s and early 1900s, a period when scientific and mathematical practice was largely, but not solely, dominated by men.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: "Our findings confirm that the UK science specifications reflect this historical imbalance: although women made significant contributions to major scientific breakthroughs, this fact is rarely acknowledged." The academics recommended that Franklin should be included "in all specifications when teaching DNA structure".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: They also said specifications should refer to Marie Curie, who discovered radium and polonium and coined the term radioactivity, and nuclear physicist Lise Meitner, who discovered nuclear fission, among others.
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Department for Education in England said "girls should see the contribution women have made in STEM", adding it was "committed to improving the school curriculum over the coming years, and as part of that will make sure every girl can see where their learning can take them".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: The Scottish Government said it was "committed to closing the gender gap in STEM and will carefully consider the findings of this research".
sentences.article_title: Only one female scientist named in GCSEs, research finds

sentences.text: Irene Breen told the BBC her business suffered a significant financial hit from the restrictions When Irene Breen got a notification in January 2025 that Instagram was removing adverts for her company's pregnancy pillows, she was confused.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: What was so offensive about a pillow?
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: She was later told on a call with Meta that the problem was the word "pregnancy".
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: "We had to scrub the word from our entire website… from the product name," Breen said.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: "We had to remove all our URLs which had pregnancy in them and rename them all." The restrictions were eventually lifted but, she said, it took 10 months of conversations with Instagram's parent company Meta - by which time her business had suffered a significant financial hit.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: Meta, which also owns Facebook, told the BBC that while businesses can run adverts that promote wellness, sexual health and reproductive products and services, there are restrictions to avoid users across countries and cultures having a negative experience.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: The company initially declined to comment on individual cases.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: After the BBC’s story was published, a spokesperson added: “The suggestion that the word 'pregnancy' cannot be used on our platforms is incorrect.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: To be clear, people can freely use the word 'pregnancy' in posts, and share and discuss pregnancy-related content.” It's not just businesses taking out paid adverts who claim their content has been unfairly restricted.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: Women's health creators and charities have told us their content has been removed, had sensitivity filters added, or had its reach suppressed - a practice known as "shadowbanning".
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: The campaign group CensHERship monitors claims that women's health content is being suppressed.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: In a report last month, it surveyed nearly 200 creators, clinical providers, health brands, charities, and educators - 96% of whom said they had experienced restrictions in some form.

sentences.text: This video can not be played The fight to say 'vagina' on social media Sensitivity filters heavily blur posts requiring users to press a button before they can see it and are usually reserved for graphic imagery - including nudity or violence.

sentences.text: Dr Carolina Are, a digital criminologist at the London School of Economics who studies social media moderation of women's content, said research shows AI is often used to flag posts that might breach platform guidelines.

sentences.text: But that can mean an "algorithm misdetecting" content, as it is created to do, storing that information to repeat "previous mistaken decisions", she warns.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: The system often uses automated messages, Are says, which can mean users are then unable to question a decision.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: "One of the hashtags, unbelievably, was #vaginalcancer." "We put a post on Instagram about vulval anatomy - it was very clearly an anatomical diagram with labels around it, talking about vulval cancer and the need to check for changes, lumps and bumps.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: It was pulled." The diagram was put behind a sensitivity filter The charity appealed, which was initially denied - but after several weeks the post "suddenly reappeared" behind a sensitivity filter.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: Lamnisos added it wasn't exaggerating to say that "life-saving health information isn't getting to the people who need it most".
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: Despite her raising this with Meta, the problem has continued, she said.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: Deirdre O'Neill, from fertility test company Hertility, said it had a similar issue with a Facebook and Instagram video featuring a woman with endometriosis.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: "She doesn't sell our services, she doesn't talk about Hertility, she simply describes her pain," O'Neill said.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: But the video was removed by Meta, she said, and classified as political content.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: Asked about Eve Appeal and Hertility's cases, Meta did not comment specifically, but said it allows women's health content on its platforms, and is consulting with women's health organisations to improve systems.

sentences.text: The post featuring a woman talking about endometriosis was flagged and classified as "social issues, elections or politics" Trying to advertise on TikTok has also become "like an obstacle course", O'Neill added.

sentences.text: Ofcom is investigating whether Meta breached its duties under the UK's online safety laws with the launch of its "Instants" feature on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: The tool - allowing users to take and share an instant image with close friends, that disappears once viewed - was launched on Meta's photo-sharing app in May as "a new way to share photos in the moment".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But the regulator said the social media giant had not properly assessed risks posed by the feature prior to launching it - something it is required to do under the UK's Online Safety Act (OSA).

sentences.text: A Meta spokesperson said in a statement that it "takes its regulatory obligations under the Online Safety Act seriously".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We conducted a risk analysis and briefed Ofcom about this feature on a number of occasions before launching it," they said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "We will of course co-operate with Ofcom during this investigation." Ofcom said its probe would examine whether Meta breached OSA duties by not carrying out "a suitable and sufficient illegal content risk assessment and children's risk assessment before the launch of Instants".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Under the UK's sweeping online safety rules, platforms including Meta must carry out and update risk assessments to comply with a range of duties, including to tackle illegal content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: They must also show how they prevent children permitted to use their services from encountering content deemed harmful for them.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: This spans material relating to pornography, or promoting self-harm or suicide - as "priority primary content" - alongside things like abusive, hateful or bullying content.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Our online safety laws are clear – significant changes to platforms must be risk assessed before they're launched," said Ofcom enforcement director George Lusty.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "This is a vital step that tech firms must take to protect their users," he added.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Images shared with Instants can be viewed by those who have been selected as "close friends" by a user, or those who they follow and are followed back by.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: Meta says the feature has a range of built-in protections, including for younger users with Teen Accounts, including preventing screenshots, reshares or forwarding of Instants.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: But disappearing messages and images have been singled out previously as posing particular risks for child or teen users of some apps .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom investigates Meta over Instagram Instants feature

sentences.text: "Safety by design must be built in, not bolted on, and today's investigation shows we'll take action where we have concerns that providers are failing to comply," Lusty added.

sentences.text: York was the subject of the city-wide pilot, which also put on workshops for parents and offered special training for early years staff.

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England are now signed up to launch similar schemes to tackle the number of pupils starting school without being fully toilet-trained.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government said the pilot's results were "encouraging", and confirmed they were committed to 75% of pupils reaching a good level of development at the end of their first year in school by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Since April this year, parents across York have been targeted via GP surgeries, pharmacies, family hubs, schools, nurseries and libraries with information and offers of support on how to potty-train their child ahead of starting school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Potty training guides were sent out to all families across York who had a child starting reception in September - with the aim that all children could use the toilet independently by the time they started school, except those with medical issues or special educational needs.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The results from all 55 mainstream primary schools across the city, shared exclusively with BBC News, suggested there had been a 43% drop since last year in the number of children who were not fully toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Across York last September, 148 out of 1,364 reception pupils (11%) were recorded as not being toilet-trained when they started school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: This year, that fell to 85 reception pupils out of 1,374 (6%).
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Parents Natalie and Lucy, who both have daughters starting reception next year, have welcomed the extra support on offer.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Mum Natalie says there's a lot of conflicting pressures on parents about the right time to potty-train Lucy said she had noticed the drop-in sessions on potty training in her local children's centre and thought it was a "really good idea".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think it's really important that children are more prepared for that aspect of starting school," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Natalie said getting her daughter Freya potty-trained in time for school has been a priority, but feels there is a lot of pressure on parents to do so.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "I think going to school is hard enough for children," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When I was little, we still had the terry towelling nappies and they had to be washed and hung on the line.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So I think with disposable nappies it's easier," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Around one in four children started school in England and Wales last year not fully toilet-trained, and teachers said they have been spending over an hour a day changing nappies, according to the latest research from the children's charity Kindred Squared , external .
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Felicity Gillespie, chief executive of Kindred Squared, told BBC Radio 4's Today programme that children not being potty trained when starting school was "a real concern for teachers".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "They tell us that they're losing, on average across the country, a day a week of teaching time to dealing with potty-training issues." Gillespie is keen to spread the message that "it's best for children to be coming out of nappies" when they are between 18 and 30 months old.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "When the teacher's leaving the class to change someone's nappy, the rest of the class is having their learning broken up.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: So everybody loses out,” she added.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The ability to listen to and follow instructions is another skill that helps pupils get the most out of learning when they start reception class Jo Mould, who teaches reception at Robert Wilkinson Primary Academy in York, said she has noticed an improvement in pupils being ready for school this year.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "We've spent more time teaching in these last three weeks than we have in previous years," she said.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "The children have come in so ready to learn, because they're more settled and regulated socially and emotionally.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: We've had a really, really positive start to the school year." Jo Mould says not having to deal with toilet training has meant more time spent teaching her pupils York councillor Bob Webb said the impact of the scheme had been "so positive" for both schools and families.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: But he acknowledged a potential "gap in support" for parents between seeing health visitors with their toddler, and the child later arriving at school.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: He said the key to the scheme's success was collaboration across health visitors, schools and other community settings, but that there was "always more that could be done at an earlier age".
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Twenty local authorities across England have now committed to adopt York's model, developed by Kindred Squared, and use it to encourage earlier potty-training in their areas.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: That means they were assessed by teachers on being able to complete tasks like going to the toilet and paying attention in class.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: The government has said it is still committed to increasing that proportion to 75% by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: Early Education Minister Paul Waugh said it was "encouraging to see this pilot helping more children develop the confidence and independence they need before starting school", stressing the importance of parents taking early steps towards toilet training.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: In York, Mould said she hopes next year's parents will take on potty-training even earlier.
sentences.article_title: Potty training scheme to roll out to 20 more areas

sentences.text: "Ideally we'd be at the point where [children] don't need that support when they get here, because they've already been trained by the time they get to us." Do you have any views, comments or questions about this story?

sentences.text: A woman convinced her former partner she had given birth to two children who most likely did not exist in what a High Court judge described as an "extraordinary" and "elaborate campaign of deceit".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The man, who has not been named but was referred to as John in the judgement, applied to the Family Court after he was told the woman had sold their two children for a combined £500.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The case heard that the man received messages and photos of the children and paid the woman around £30,000 over the course of two years.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: But in a hearing in February, the woman, who was referred to as Jane, told the judge she had lied about the pregnancies for revenge, claiming the man had abused her.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The court heard the man believed he was the children's' father because in late 2022 his partner told him she was pregnant, sent pictures of an ultrasound image and had become "visibly pregnant" as time went on.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In May 2023, shortly before the first baby was due, the woman called the police alleging she had been assaulted by the man.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: He was arrested and subsequently held on remand for several months, Mrs Justice Judd said in her ruling which was published on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Following this, the woman sent a message to his stepfather saying the baby had been born as well as sharing baby photos.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: At one stage she is said to have sent voice notes to her former partner's mother in the middle of the night with the sound of a baby crying in the background.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: Later, she told the man she was pregnant again and the baby was due in August 2024.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: However, before the due date, the couple split up and did not reconcile.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman would go on to tell the man's mother the baby had been born.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The woman admitted to the court she had told him she was pregnant when they were together, and afterwards, but conceded she had told a series of elaborate lies and that there were, in fact, no children.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She argued she was menopausal at the time and could not have been pregnant and bank statements show she attended a tanning shop on the day she said she had given birth, Mrs Justice Judd said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: In her judgement, the judge concluded that the "factors that weigh against the children genuinely existing were very strong, stronger than the factors pointing the other way".
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: She said the man was the victim of a "sustained and elaborate campaign of deceit" which also impacted his mother and closest friend.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: "Added to this, the behaviour was cruel, leading a man and his mother to believe they had children and grandchildren respectively.", the Judge said.
sentences.article_title: Woman deceived ex-partner that she had given birth to his babies, judge rules

sentences.text: The judge added she was unable to conclude the woman's motive for her behaviour but said financial fraud was a "possibility"  and that the "complex mental health problems" she suffered from may have also played a part.

sentences.text: Children should be introduced to the world of work at the start of primary school, says the author of a major report into youth activity in the UK.

sentences.text: Former minister Alan Milburn says children as young as four should be learning about different careers, with work experience placements made mandatory for 14- to 16-year-olds.

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: The latest data from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) suggests 981,000 people aged 16 to 24 in the UK were not in education, employment or training (known as Neet), between April and June 2026.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "It'd be good if employers came into schools and said, 'Look, this is what's going on, these are things that are possible.'" Milburn says that for Key Stage 4 pupils - aged between 14 and 16 - experience must be given in a real workplace with employer feedback.

sentences.text: "Work experience needs to be mandatory.

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Emma, from Kirklees, has grandchildren in Years 1, 2 and 4 and thinks primary school is too young to be introducing careers talks.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "In primary school, there is too much trying to get little kids to grow up too quickly," she says.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: "Just let them be little kids.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: I know they have to learn and the world's changing, but still, give them a chance to be kids." But Zoe, another parent, disagrees.
sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.article_title: Employers should teach primary-age children about work, says Milburn

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools and colleges in England will be required to recognise antisemitism as a distinct category of harm and take explicit action against it.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It means anti-Jewish hatred will be treated as a specific safeguarding risk rather than being dealt with through existing measures to stop racism and bullying.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The government has accepted all of the 27 recommendations made in the government-commissioned review including dedicated training for teachers and more consistent recording of incidents.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says The review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England was led by former Ofsted chief inspector Sir David Bell and presented to Parliament on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC it marked a "generational moment" to re-educate young people, among whom she said the issue of antisemitism was "particularly prevalent".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the House of Commons "teachers should not bring their own political views into the classroom" but they should not avoid discussing important topics.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review was launched following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025, in which two men were killed.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Separate reviews were also commissioned into antisemitism in healthcare and into public order and hate crime laws.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters .
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also recommends that the government sets up a type of hotline where school leaders can access immediate advice on tackling antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Bell, who is now vice-chancellor of the University of Sunderland, heard evidence from pupils, teachers, governors and parents across state and independent schools, as well as from community organisations.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: He told the BBC: "This is not just a report for Jewish children in Jewish schools.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This is for all children and young people in all schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: We know that antisemitism crosses all boundaries." Earlier this month, the BBC was given rare access inside a Jewish school in Hertfordshire, where pupils and staff operate under tight security, amid heightened concerns about antisemitism.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: A second head teachers' union has called for a halt to graded Ofsted inspections in England, saying it is "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale" of its members.

sentences.text: The Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL) also raised the prospect of potential strike action, saying a new grading system had become an "overbearing mess".

sentences.text: ASCL's announcement comes after another union, the National Association of Head Teachers (NAHT) , said changes Ofsted made to inspections just under a year ago had been severely harmful to school leaders' welfare.
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: ASCL said it had passed a motion of no confidence in "the ability of Ofsted's leadership to address the damage being done by the new inspection system", adding that it was "increasingly concerned about the welfare and morale of members".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary, said the union did not take the step "lightly", but added Ofsted's "warm words about recognising wellbeing pressures... have not been matched by the action necessary" and that "negotiation [had] hit a brick wall".
sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.text: "The current system is not fit for purpose.

sentences.article_title: Ofsted faces fresh calls to halt graded school inspections in England

sentences.article_title: Changes to GCSE Maths 'pulling the rug out from under pupils'

sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Microsoft boss Satya Nadella says he has not seen anything like the PHP emergency "in a long, long time".
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Referencing the ongoing global efforts to fix the critical cyber-security flaw in millions of websites, he told a conference "it was a long day and a long night, I know, for all the IT and security folks".
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Other IT and cyber experts have told the BBC about their struggles in the last 48 hours, whose stories give us an insight into what it is like at the coalface of a major cyber emergency.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But also highlight how misinformation and panic has made things a lot worse.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "It's been relentless," says UK-based system administrator Adam Mudd.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said he had never had so many messages from people who were worried about their websites.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "The biggest challenge has been juggling clients who want their sites taken offline as a precaution, while trying to coordinate updates and fixes across countless different setups," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Sometimes it takes me longer to take a website down than to fix the PHP problem." PHP is a very popular programming language which powers millions of websites.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But two critical flaws were found with the system that led to the emergency response, with national cyber-security authorities urging IT teams to download a security fix urgently or take websites and servers offline.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Mudd says since then he has been under enormous pressure and has lost a huge amount of sleep - working early and not finishing until 22:30 BST to secure his customers' systems.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: In Mauritius, IT administrator Loganaden Velvindron said he too was flat out since his team realised just how much software relies on PHP.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Many versions of php running are completely end-of-life, so we are having to rebuilding web apps and change code in some cases," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said part of the problem was the announcement about the security vulnerabilities in PHP came as a surprise, without much time to prepare for action.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Jon Jones, Technical director for a digital advertising company, was also spurred into action by the alerts.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "Seeing the warning drop was definitely eye-opening and a new experience we've not dealt with before," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "But, in a way, it was exciting feeling like a bit of a Hollywood action scene." The PHP Foundation, which manages the programming language, released its software fix and there was a scramble for people to download it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: Jones said it felt like "the race was on" when the patch launched at 15:00 BST on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "It was also a bit nerve-racking as anyone who has applied software updates before would know, there's always a chance than an update can cause other issues," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: The rush came as someone had leaked details of the PHP flaw early - and it was heavily rumoured that cyber-criminals were already trying to carry out attacks.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But cyber experts are also now questioning whether or not those rumours were real.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "We were flooded with rubbish intel about hackers being out there actively with working Proof of Concept (PoC) methods," said UK cyber expert Daniel Card.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said he also been flat out since Tuesday when the rumours of PHP hacks began circulating.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "This isn't the first time we've had a situation like this but it feels like it's been on another dimension," he said.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He agreed that on paper the PHP vulnerabilities were very serious and should be taken seriously, but he and many others are frustrated with the misinformation about hackers being on the loose.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: As well as the alerts from government agencies - even the Prime Minister of Japan - cyber-security companies also made errors which didn't help.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: One major firm in this space issued warnings saying hackers had a working PoC - only to have to retract it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: In spite of warnings from Cloudflare and AWS that "millions of hacking attempts" had been made every hour, there is also no evidence of large scale data breaches or cyber-attacks.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: It is true that hackers have been seen to use AI to attempt to build attack methods, but none of them seem to be working at scale at the moment - something that may well change soon.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: AI was also used to find the PHP flaws which had been hidden from human researchers for decades.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: The IT workers we spoke to all agreed that these kinds of serious flaws were going to be uncovered more frequently now that AI tools had become so good at hacking.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: But some in the industry are concerned about how people were told about the critical vulnerabilities in PHP, as they fear improvements in AI will throw up more incidents like it.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: "We're going to find scary vulnerabilities with the amazing capabilities that OpenAI and Anthropic are bringing online, but we need to calibrate the messaging," posted Mark Maunder, founder of Wordfence - a Wordpress security tool.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble

sentences.text: He said there was a risk of "alert fatigue" which could be a big problem if a fully exploitable and serious vulnerability arose.
sentences.article_title: 'It's been relentless' say IT workers on frontline of PHP cyber-security scramble
