sentences.text: I once worked opposite a site where a shopping centre was being built.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: We were warned there might be unexploded bombs from World War Two unearthed during the construction.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: In the end, there were none, but procedures were put in place as a precaution and we all had to practice filing into designated safe zones inside our building.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: The PHP story feels like the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb - I have never seen such a dramatic, public and global response to a cyber event that hasn't happened yet.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: There has been no painful attack like the ransomware we saw knock out M&S and JLR in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: But the potential threat is so serious that websites around the world have been taken down as a precaution.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: Less than two months ago , 100 tech companies wrote an open letter warning the world to adopt a new level of cyber resilience in the age of AI.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: It turns out we didn't have to wait very long to find out what they meant.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: The weaknesses found in the PHP programming language, which is used by millions of websites, had been quietly resting there for years and are not easy to exploit.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: One cyber security researcher told me he'd been up all night trying to do it as an experiment, but it was proving very difficult.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: However, things that are very difficult for humans are increasingly very little trouble for AI.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: The tech is getting a lot of credit here for assisting researchers in finding the bugs, and the PHP foundation, which oversees the programming language, was on the case and issued a fix.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: It was supposed to be kept quiet until everyone had a chance to fix their sites - but the news was leaked.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: From that point the clock started ticking.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: As I write this, there are no reports that anyone or anything has succeeded in using the flaws to attack a site.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "There's a real dilemma," said Prof Alan Woodward from Surrey University.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "How do you alert people they need to be ready, and then that a patch is urgently required, whilst not alerting attackers?
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "Basically you're telling everyone about the problem at the same time and hoping the defenders aren't awake enough to act as soon as the patch is out." But we do know from large web companies like Cloudflare and Palo Alto Networks that millions of attempts have been made.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: We probably won't know for a while whether it has worked for any criminals, because the companies affected might not be aware yet either.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: As far as we know the unexploded bomb remains intact for now, and for some experts this is a success.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: Gina Neff, Professor of Responsible AI at Queen Mary University, described this as a good news story.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "We've seen how a team of people supported by the large AI company have used AI to find the problem, work for months together to solve it and get everybody ready to be safe and secure," she told the Today Programme on BBC Radio 4.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: "We have enormous capability to handle these risks." But the baddies can use AI too, and those same tools are probably churning away right now trying to get in.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: Cyber security authorities are warning website owners to fix the weaknesses immediately, but the patch only works on the latest version of PHP, so older sites will need to upgrade first.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: For many it may be a significant repair job, so if there's a web developer in your life you may want to send them thoughts, prayers and maybe a strong coffee.
sentences.article_title: Zoe Kleinman: PHP is the cyber equivalent of an unexploded bomb

sentences.text: The UK government says it is working to identify any potential exposure in its online services, after critical cyber-security flaws were identified in the PHP programming language that underpins a significant number of the world's websites.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Governments and some of the world's biggest companies are rushing to protect systems that use PHP before hackers can exploit the flaws.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The flaws were first discovered by AI, after which governments urged anyone who uses PHP to address them.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: A UK government spokesperson urged "all organisations, private and public, large and small" to follow guidance to protect their systems.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia, earlier urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a statement. , external Amazon said its threat intelligence system identified it was targeted on Saturday.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: It added there were further "exploitation attempts" once the embargo on the flaw warning was lifted.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The company said it "automatically detected and restricted malicious scanning attempts targeting this vulnerability." PHP powers a vast number of platforms, including online shops, Wikipedia and WordPress – the content management system behind many websites like blogs.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: When you visit a website like Wikipedia, PHP is the code that collects information you need and presents it in a way you can read on the web.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Surrey Centre for Cyber Security Prof Alan Woodward said the flaw affects some 30 million websites.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: As well as the scale of the flaw, Woodward said the nature of it means "an attacker can get their own code on to the webserver and run it and basically do whatever they like." "They can steal data , they can go to other parts of your network.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: All sort of things like that - even plant a backdoor to get in later on, so it's pretty serious," Woodward told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: This video can not be played Why have websites around the world been taken down?
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: BBC explains Cyber security researcher Ryan Austin, who has been researching PHP security for the last 20 years, said he discovered the flaw in the programming language.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: He told the Today programme it was "the most serious vulnerability I've ever found" which "started with a hunch that I would not have been able to scratch without AI".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Austin described PHP as "one of the first web languages that powered the early internet".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: "It's in a lot of places that you wouldn't expect to be that are basically very core to how the internet runs in a lot of ways.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: It's like all the old things that are in a house that you know keeps it [running] but you don't really think about," the PHP researcher said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: But Austin said this incident is not necessarily bad news because organisations would now "run and patch PHP immediately" if they haven't already.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Listen to BBC Radio 4 Today programme on BBC Sounds Amazon announced on Wednesday that it had identified a "PHP2Shell exploitation attempt" that occurred on 17 October.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: In the attack, an anonymous internet address attempted to target weaknesses in one of Amazon's decoy or "honeypot" systems, the company's security chief CJ Moses said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The use of an anonymous IP address suggests that the activity was conducted by a "threat actor", he said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: While the PHP Foundation intended to release its discovery later this month along with a complete fix for the problem, usually referred to by software developers as a "patch", details of the flaw were leaked on social media on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: In subsequent attacks on Amazon that occurred on 21 October, "the actual payloads and choices in anonymisation infrastructure varied, suggesting these were multiple actors," Moses said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The attacks occurred after the leak, but before the embargo was lifted on the PHP warning.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The use of AI means that "more actors can act within hours or even minutes once technical details of a vulnerability are disclosed", Moses added.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The PHP incident has "demonstrated how quickly AI is changing our cybersecurity landscape", Australian Council on AI Strategy CEO Anna-Maria Arabia told the BBC, as "what used to take months, to expose a vulnerability, is now taking days".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: She warned that threats would only become more commonplace as AI technology rapidly improves.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: It is "not going backwards, in other words", she said.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The PHP flaws went undetected for at least a decade.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Cyber-security firm Wiz has estimated that "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to independently verify that figure.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The websites for several BBC programmes including Doctor Who and The Traitors are currently inaccessible.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, "in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Edinburgh and Oxford council websites also went offline on Wednesday, but are now accessible.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: What is PHP and why did it spark a global cyber security scramble?
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The Dutch cybersecurity agency went offline as a precaution, and Finland's government shut down its public web services.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Wikipedia also took down parts of its website.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: This was in line with advice issued by governments, including the US, to take websites down if the flaws could not immediately be fixed.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: The US National Security Agency said that the vulnerabilities identified "often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: It could allow attackers to "steal sensitive data, disrupt services, or move deeper into a network.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: These vulnerabilities are flaws in PHP itself, not in the hosted application or its configuration," the NSA said in a later update.
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: OpenAI called the discovery, "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory".
sentences.article_title: UK working to identify exposure after global cyber-security warning

sentences.text: Irish DJ Jazzy is best known for tracks like No Bad Vibes and Somedays Releasing your first album is a big step for any artist, but for Jazzy it's one that's followed some huge strides.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: The Irish singer and DJ has been streamed more than a billion times and worked with industry heavyweights including Calvin Harris.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: If that's not enough, on Saturday she has her biggest gig yet when she'll be playing tracks like No Bad Vibes and Someday in front of a home crowd in Dublin.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: For Jazzy, writing an album has always been in the back of her mind and now, finally, it's time to hit send.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: She's previously released dozens of singles, building up a monthly listenership over 10 million strong, but Peace and Patience is her first full-length work.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: "It's been quite a few years of creating some smaller projects," she tells BBC Newsbeat.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: "That's given me enough experience now to feel like it was the right moment." The 30-year-old, real name Yasmine Byrne, has been putting out music for more than five years and collabed with the likes of Sonny Fodera, Rossi. and KILIMANJARO on some of her biggest tracks.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: Dance music has boomed in recent years, with Spotify previously telling Newsbeat that since 2020 the amount under-25s listen to the genre has grown by more than 73% globally.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: It also dominated festival line-ups over the summer - including Radio 1's Big Weekend which dedicated all its stages to dance music on the opening night.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: But artists in the genre have often moved away from albums, opting instead to release EPs and singles.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: Jazzy has noticed the change, saying it feels "a lot different now, with people kind of siding with virality rather than quality of music".
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: "When I was making the album, I wasn't thinking about going viral or anything like that.
sentences.article_title: The artist dropping her debut album after a billion streams

sentences.text: Matilda The Musical is celebrating 15 years since its debut in London A musical that began life as a Christmas production in Stratford-upon-Avon has become one of the biggest theatre successes of the century as it celebrates 15 years in London's West End.
sentences.article_title: Matilda celebrates 15 years as West End success story

sentences.text: A mysterious caped figure has been helping the people of London.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Not dealing with the criminal hi-jinks of The Joker or Catwoman (thankfully), instead doing good deeds for others: paying for fuel at petrol stations, helping people across busy roads and even filling in potholes.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: These may not be the type of do-gooder acts that sell comic books, but London's Batman, as they are known, has already got 297k followers on TikTok and their posts have had more 2m likes since they first appeared at the end of September.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Despite the capital’s hero doing their best to make people’s days a little brighter, one question keeps hounding them: who are they?
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Can they be like Bruce and keep their identity secret, or will they soon be unmasked?
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Socials are awash with the theory that London's Batman is none other than Niko Omilana, known for posting prank videos on socials and as a contestant on the first series of The Celebrity Traitors .
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Niko appears to be the most popular candidate for London Batman’s secret identity as he has a reputation for pranks which take a lot of organisation and can involve handing out goods to people.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: In 2021, he opened a fake store in the city and gave away free smartphones to the public as his comment on what he saw as the high price of technology.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Niko posted a short video of himself on TikTok showing he was in the heart of New York, a move some people interpreted as him trying to prove he is not London’s Batman.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: That hasn’t stopped others trying to prove otherwise.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Comments on the post suggest it could have been pre-recorded as the theatre advertisements behind him don’t reflect the ones playing in the city at the moment, although this hasn’t been verified.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: TikTok user officialroyce1 posted that Niko’s video was meaningless as he could have flown to New York and back in the same day to cover his tracks.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: At the moment, there are lots of theories but absolutely no evidence that Niko is dressing up as a superhero and helping out in the community.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: A similar situation happened earlier this year when some posters on socials were convinced that the Liverpool rapper EsDeeKid was really the actor Timothee Chalamet in disguise .
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: This was later disproved after the theory went viral.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: Until London’s Batman pulls back their mask to reveal their secret identity, we can’t say for sure.
sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.article_title: Who is London’s Batman? Is it Niko Omilana?

sentences.text: The BBC's announcement that it will close three of its linear broadcast channels - BBC Three, BBC Scotland and Radio 4 Extra - makes sense financially.

sentences.text: BBC Three's most popular show on Monday night was a repeat of an old episode of Top Gear.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: Around 77,000 people tuned in.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: BBC Scotland's TV channel was watched, according to this year's annual report, by a weekly average of 12% of the Scottish population.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: The same goes for BBC Three, although the hokey cokey that has gone on with that channel - launched to fanfare in 2003, later made digital-only, then brought back to linear in 2022, now back online only again - has looked indecisive.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: But the bigger picture is that viewers and listeners are already migrating online - increasingly finding the BBC's programmes not via those linear TV and radio channels but on iPlayer, BBC Sounds, and, more recently, YouTube.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: So that's the business case - and the BBC needs to save £500m over the next three years.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: That figure is concentrating minds.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: But axing the three linear channels is a drop in the ocean financially.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: I understand it will save less than £10m in total per year.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: BBC Three launched hits including Normal People, starring Paul Mescal and Daisy Edgar-Jones Last year the BBC spent £42m creating content for BBC Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: It still plans to create many of those shows for iPlayer - and BBC Two in Scotland will be reconfigured to deliver Scotland-only programming.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: The part of BBC Three that commissions programmes will actually get more money to spend on creating content aimed specifically at 16-34s (with a core focus on the 16-25s).
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: This was the network that commissioned Normal People, Fleabag, Killing Eve - programmes of quality and wide appeal.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: There's also been a recent announcement of commissions dreamt up specifically for YouTube - to reach those 16-24s who the BBC (and other public service broadcasters) find so difficult to lure to their own platforms.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: Many of Radio 4 Extra's programmes will also still be on BBC Sounds.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: If you listen to the Daily Service, first broadcast in 1928 and the longest-running programme of its kind anywhere in the world, you will still be able to find it.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: So these aren't major cost savings.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: The BBC would likely argue, when it comes to audiences, who are at the heart of everything, it is pivoting to find them where they already are.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: What's been announced today is more about the direction of travel.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: It's about the continuing evolution of the BBC, a streamlining as audience habits change.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: That doesn't mean it isn't painful to all of us inside the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: Job cuts are always difficult.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: In News, 100 more roles are being axed.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: That's on top of the 200 already announced.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: And the news division is still nowhere near its target of £51m of cuts.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: And with only two fifths of the £500m of total savings now announced, there is still a very long way to go.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: As a BBC user, you are going to hear much more about cuts in the coming months.
sentences.article_title: Katie Razzall: BBC closures make business sense, but far more savings are needed

sentences.text: African diaspora is finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage A new sound is taking Bristol's dancefloors by storm.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Driven by rolling log drums, syncopated rhythms and infectious melodies, amapiano and other electronic sounds from across the African diaspora are finding new audiences in a city celebrated for its musical heritage.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Behind these parties is a new generation of black promoters passionate about creating spaces where black people can hear their music, celebrate their cultures and feel like they belong.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But for some, building these spaces has also meant confronting the familiar challenge of finding spaces where black music and the communities around it are welcomed and not feared.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Unkle Mykel started hosting events to connect to different cultures Bristol-based promoter Unkle Mykel's journey into events began in his own back garden after he moved to Bristol in 2017.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: What started as garden barbecues gradually grew into a way of bringing people together, particularly members of Bristol's black, Asian and minority ethnic communities.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's about celebrating our cultures, bringing people into that fold and connecting," says the 32-year-old, who hosts Bristol Barbecue Family and The Aux Social.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Originally from Kenya, Mykel moved to the UK in 2005.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Since then, he has witnessed changes in the visibility of African music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There was no Afrobeats on the airwaves," he laughs, recalling his early years in the country, when he says Caribbean reggae, dancehall and soca were more prominent in the musical landscape he encountered.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Now, he sees the growing popularity of genres such as amapiano - a popular South African house music subgenre - as an opportunity to broaden the scene.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We don't need to pretend to be nobody else, we're just us.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: It just took a while to get there." DJ and promoter Khiah Lou runs amapiano event called Khaya Nights For 30-year-old DJ and promoter Khiah Lou, representation, she says, is central to her work.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Last year she launched Khaya Nights, an event dedicated to amapiano and other African Caribbean electronic dance music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Having performed internationally, she had seen how other cities had developed a wider range of events celebrating these sounds.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Bristol, she felt, was lagging behind.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Rather than wait for the scene to develop, Khiah decided to help build it herself.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "If we don't do it, who else is going to do it?" she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Young black people are starting to make a way for themselves because I don't think we have a choice." Khiah says these nights provide a place where people can connect with their identities and see their cultures reflected in the city around them.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "At first it seems like it's just a party, but it's so much more than that," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It's really important for your own self-identity.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: If your community doesn't have events, where do you feel you can go?" "At first it seems like just a party, but it's so much more than that,' says Khiah Tazmin Samuels, who DJs as Azumei, shares those concerns about representation.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: As part of Rushtown, a black-led music collective, Tazmin wants to champion sounds and subcultures from across Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "My main motivation for getting together with people and starting Rushtown came from seeing the lack of representation of black music that black people are currently listening to within the city," says Tazmin.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: She sees encouraging signs, with more black music-focused brands emerging in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: But she believes the wider music industry has yet to recognise the value of what these promoters are building.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Tazmin says the wider music industry must recognise the value of black promoters But creating these spaces is not always straightforward.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Khiah says she has struggled to find venues willing to host nights aimed at black audiences.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Although she considers Bristol an inclusive city, her experience as a promoter has revealed a different side of its nightlife.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I've had some venue owners straight up tell me they're worried about having a black event," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "I feel like black crowds are kind of met with fear, and that's really disheartening." Mykel describes similar tensions, saying that some venues are enthusiastic about hosting his events, only to face objections from people in the surrounding community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: The Bamboo Club opened in 1966 as a social hub for Bristol's Caribbean community The young promoters' experiences echo a much longer history of black Bristolians having to create their own spaces for music and social life.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Many black people were turned away from existing clubs and bars in Bristol during the 1960s, which led to the creation of  "blues parties", un-licensed house parties where people danced to genres such as ska, reggae and rocksteady.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: In 1966, Tony Bullimore and his Jamaican-born wife Lalel, opened the Bamboo Club, which served as a cultural lifeline for the city's Caribbean community.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Glen Crooks, 70, who used to perform at the Bamboo Club when he was younger, remembers "sneaking in" with his friends when they were young.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was the only place that we could have," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Especially all the Caribbean people could go and really have a good time." Rushtown aims to champion a variety of music genres from the African diaspora Marti Burgess, who has been a co-owner of the nightclub Lakota since 1994, says although attitudes have changed over the years, some prejudices remain.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "There is a long history of treating a predominantly black audience as a concern, rather than recognising the audience, creativity and business that a promoter is bringing," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "They should not have to keep proving that black audiences are welcome or commercially worthwhile." Growing up, Marti was surrounded by music.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: Her parents went to the blues clubs and attended the Bamboo Club when it hosted artists such as Bob Marley, Desmond Dekker and Johnny Nash.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "It was through listening to the adults' conversations that I came to understand how much those spaces had grown out of exclusion from mainstream venues," she says.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "Latino Fest this summer opened our eyes further to the audiences and musical communities we could welcome," says Marti.
sentences.article_title: The rise of new black spaces in music

sentences.text: "We want people across the different genres of black music to see Lakota as a venue that is open to them, where they can bring their music and their audiences." Follow BBC Bristol on Facebook , external , X , external and Instagram , external .

sentences.text: Kgomotso Mathekga says a lack of male role models is fuelling violence against women in his neighbourhood "I witness men hitting women all the time," says Kgomotso Mathekga, 30.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Especially when they are both drunk." "I once had an argument with my girlfriend," he admits, "and I grabbed and slapped her." Mathekga is speaking frankly during a gathering of men aimed at helping reduce the high levels of violence against women in South Africa.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The meeting is held in a narrow street in a Johannesburg informal settlement known as Organic Market.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: It is a maze of corrugated metal shacks and unpaved roads, close to Alexandra township.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Now I feel pain," Mathekga continues.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We broke up and I no longer see my child.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: I feel like I've contributed to the problems in South Africa, instead of being the gentleman that I know I am." At a nearby tavern, a group of men have pulled their chairs into a circle in the dust.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: At the centre stands Itumeleng Stephen Tamaga, known locally as Bra Steve.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The group clap and cheers.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "Listen guys," Bra Steve says.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We must stand together to fight against gender-based violence and femicide." Bra Steve is the local organiser of Father A Nation, a non-profit that works with men and boys to promote positive masculinity and help end violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The group's meeting comes as South Africa grapples with renewed anger over renewed cases of femicide and violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The discovery of the bodies of 12 women over three months, in the city of Ekurhuleni, near Johannesburg has reignited questions about the scale of what many people see as being a crisis of violence against women.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: Bra Steve says: "We must restore dignity to the men around here" South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa has acknowledged that his government has not done enough and announced measures he hopes can make women feel safer.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: The country has one of the highest murder rates in the world, with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: In that period, according to the South African Human Rights Commission, 569 women were killed, an average of six a day, and 1,052 others survived attempted murder.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: A report in 2022 by the Human Sciences Research Council found that more than 35% of South African women experienced physical or sexual violence, many from their own intimate partners.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: For Bra Steve, part of the solution to the crisis is helping men to understand the issue and take responsibility for their actions.
sentences.article_title: The South African men trying to end violence against women: 'Every man needs to play a part'

sentences.text: "We are a lost generation," he says.

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: There are few better words than "apocalyptic" to describe the way this looks.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "Sometimes at night my baby's chest makes a rattling sound," she says.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "Those thoughts haunt me every night." Nastiti lives in Palangkaraya, at the frontline of a months-long environmental catastrophe that has blanketed large parts of Southeast Asia in a toxic haze.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Wildfires have torched some 1.9 million hectares across Indonesia since the start of the year, according to open-access satellite platform Nusantara Atlas – an area roughly the size of the US state of New Jersey, or the entire landmass of Fiji.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: One million hectares are thought to have burned in September alone.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: But the toxic fallout is larger still.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Swathes of smouldering forest, swamp and peatlands have turned the air thick with microparticles and carbon monoxide, creating a noxious cloud that has swaddled Indonesia and drifted as far as Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: As of mid-October, Indonesia's Health Ministry had recorded more than 277,000 cases of people suffering from chronic coughs and acute respiratory infections.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: More than 62,000 of those were infants and toddlers under the age of five.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "The forest fires have had a huge impact, especially on everyone's health," says 22-year-old Natari Victoria, who was admitted to a health centre in Palangkarya after suffering from a cough for more than a week.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "I have young cousins, including babies, who are coughing too.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: It's really taking a toll on them." Dianyra Eka Nastiti is worried about how her children will recover Haze and smoke from peat fires contain a complex mixture of pollutants that pose serious health risks to the human body.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Among these are tiny microparticles which can penetrate deep into the lungs and, in some cases, enter the bloodstream, causing inflammation, chronic lung diseases and increased risk of premature death.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Another concern is the toxic greenhouse gases that are being unleashed into the air.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "Here in Central Kalimantan, especially in Palangkaraya, the sky has turned yellow and hazy," says Riduan, head of the Palangkaraya Health Office.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "So what are the residents actually breathing in?
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: It's not fresh oxygen; it's carbon dioxide and pollutants.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: And what happens as a result?
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: The body – specifically the brain – doesn't get enough oxygen." Children, older adults and pregnant women are particularly vulnerable to the dangers of haze, especially during prolonged periods of exposure, when the health impacts can accumulate.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: In places like Palangkarya, the official advice is to stay indoors and avoid going out.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "It's simply not possible, and I feel like the people who say things like that have no idea what is actually happening here." Nastiti's utmost priority, however, is the health and wellbeing of her children.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: And when the haze grows heavy, she is quick to force them inside.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "With conditions being so unsafe, I have no choice," she says.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "Our young children should be at the park, playing with their friends and going to school.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Instead, they are locked inside the house." Lola Macitri, a 37-year-old who lives in the rural village of Ramang, 50km (31 miles) north of Palangkaraya, has been similarly housebound.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: As the smog has deepened over the past few weeks – from dusty grey to amber yellow and, more recently, burnt orange – she and her family have come to spend most of their time indoors.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Her children, like many others in Indonesia's more haze-affected areas, have been doing their school classes online, she says, while she and other adults struggle to manage half-a-day's work out in the poisonous air.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: People have been turning up at hospitals after complaining of feeling sick from the toxic smog Countless farmers, daily-wage earners and small vendors have similarly been forced to either sacrifice their livelihoods or endure the risk of stepping outside.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: Beyond that, many are left with no choice but to wait out the storm.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "If you ask whether we are afraid of the health risks, of course we are.

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.text: "We just have to endure and stay strong through this situation, because there is simply no other option." The government is under mounting pressure from the public to do more to stop the fires, with many criticising what they see as a woefully inadequate response by the authorities.
sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze

sentences.article_title: Borneo burning: Life on the frontline of South East Asia's toxic haze
